test_name: Stun Lock overheat fails on left arm and blast waves - ebb4e2d2-bcf4-4a6a-8f32-c8ce328f69e7
summary: Neither failure has a cause I could find in the current code, so no code was changed. Stun Lock (OverStun addon, 'Addon - Stun Crashers.asset') adds an outgoing DamageModifier to the arm entity that converts Stun duration into Overheat. A Stun duration only exists on the stun-meter-fill interaction from GameEntity.AddStunDamage. That interaction is sourced from the hit's source entity and runs with ProcessingFlags.All, so outgoing modifiers do run on it. For punches the source is SP_PlayerPunchBehavior on the effector. For blast waves it is BlastwaveManager.Shockwave, whose entity is the BlastwaveArmAttachment effector. In both cases the source entity is an entity child of the arm, so sourceEntity.IsChildOf(arm) holds. The INCOMING-only flag on the shockwave's own interaction (BlastwaveManager.cs:376) only blocks Stun Lock from that interaction, which carries zero-duration Stun, so it does not explain the failure. Arm, effector and addon setup in SP_PlayerMech/ArmDef/ArmEffectorDef/SP_MechArm/SP_MechArmsController is symmetric between left and right. Changing the processing flags or the IsChildOf check without a confirmed cause would risk double-applying outgoing modifiers to every blast wave.
instructions:
Bug: the "Stun Lock" effect (stunned enemies should be treated as Overheated for damage purposes) does not reliably work when the Stun Lock modifier is socketed in the Left arm socket, and it also fails for blast-wave hits (e.g. the Focused Blaster's blast wave) regardless of which arm the modifier is socketed in. Investigate both issues, find the root cause of each, and fix them. Do not read any conversation history, chat logs, commit history, or other tool that shows previous fixes/changes made by other people in this repo — work only from the current state of the code.

Context to help you find the relevant code (do not treat this as the full answer — verify by reading the actual code):

1. Blast-wave hits (Focused Blaster and any other blast-wave damage source): look at BlastwaveManager.cs, roughly around line 360, where processingFlags appears to be forced to an "incoming" value. Check GameEntity.cs around line 2952, which appears to skip ProcessModifyOutgoingInteraction when processing flags indicate an incoming-only interaction. If Stun Lock's damage modifier is implemented as an outgoing-only modifier, it would never get a chance to run for blast-wave hits because of this flag handling. Confirm this is actually what's happening and fix it so Stun Lock's overheat conversion applies to blast-wave damage too, without breaking other outgoing/incoming modifier behavior.

2. Left-arm-only failure ("only Jack gets overheat after a hit to the face", implying the right arm or body hits work but left arm hits from the socketed modifier do not): check SP_PlayerMech's SetupArm/SetupSlot logic — there does not appear to be an explicit left/right asymmetry there, so look more specifically at how the Stun Lock DamageModifier determines which arm's hits it should convert. It appears to use something like IsChildOf to walk up from the hit's damage source to check whether the hit originated from the arm/slot the modifier is socketed on. Find why this check fails or behaves inconsistently when the modifier is socketed on the left arm specifically, and fix the parentage/source check so the modifier correctly applies to hits coming from either arm it is socketed on.

Definition of done: stunned enemies reliably become Overheated when hit by an attack from a Stun Lock modifier socketed in the left arm, the same as when socketed in the right arm. Stunned enemies also become Overheated when hit by blast-wave damage (e.g. Focused Blaster's blast wave), from either arm socket. No regressions to other outgoing/incoming damage modifiers or to normal (non-blast-wave) damage processing.
not_done: Left-arm Stun Lock fix: in code, the left and right arms take the same setup path and entity parenting. A runtime check is needed: with Stun Lock on the left arm, break at GameEntity.AddStunDamage (GameEntity.cs:871). Check whether source.entity.IsChildOf(<left SP_MechArm>) is true and whether the left arm's behaviors list contains the DamageModifier. ChangeProcessingOrder defers its Remove/AddBehavior while an interaction is being processed, which is an unverified lead.

Blast-wave Stun Lock fix: the stun-meter-fill interaction a shockwave triggers is sourced from the arm's effector and runs with ProcessingFlags.All. Removing the INCOMING-only flag would also re-apply every outgoing arm modifier to blast-wave damage that already went through outgoing processing on the generation interaction. A runtime check is needed: log whether DamageModifier.ModifyOutgoingInteraction runs on the meter-fill interaction after a Focused Blaster wave stuns an enemy, and what additionalDamageList contains.
